editorial_rule: Cases are bounded records of published methods or official lifecycle behavior. Reported results remain scoped to the source setup; no entry is a universal recipe or an invented production outcome.

cases.title: Transformer attention as the mechanism boundary
cases.problem: Sequence modeling required a mechanism that could relate token positions without recurrence.
cases.context: The 2017 Transformer experiments in machine translation.
constraints: Published experimental tasks and hardware
Predates modern chat post-training and long-context serving
cases.architecture: Encoder-decoder stacks built from multi-head attention and position-wise feed-forward layers.
cases.approach: Replace recurrent computation with attention plus positional information.
tradeoffs: Parallel training advantages
Attention cost grows with sequence length in the original formulation
failures_or_risks: The paper does not establish current product behavior, truthfulness, or safety
cases.reported_outcomes: Reported competitive translation quality with lower training cost for the evaluated configurations.
lessons: Mechanism knowledge supports debugging but does not predict a configured application's behavior
cases.limitations: Research benchmark evidence, not a production deployment case.

cases.title: Relevant information can be lost in the middle
cases.problem: Long input capacity was being treated as equivalent to reliable use of all included information.
cases.context: Controlled multi-document question answering and key-value retrieval tests across model families.
constraints: Specific models and tasks
Results do not define every current model's context behavior
cases.architecture: Prompts with relevant evidence placed at different positions in long contexts.
cases.approach: Hold task content approximately constant while varying relevant-information position.
tradeoffs: Longer context can include more evidence
More included tokens can increase cost and do not guarantee use
failures_or_risks: Performance often degraded when evidence appeared in the middle
cases.reported_outcomes: The paper reported position-sensitive performance and a primacy/recency pattern for tested models.
lessons: Budget and structure context deliberately
Evaluate evidence position and distractors
cases.limitations: Transfer to a new model or application requires fresh measurement.

cases.title: Retrieval-augmented generation separates memory from evidence supply
cases.problem: Parametric models alone make provenance and knowledge updates difficult.
cases.context: The original RAG formulation for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks.
constraints: Research corpora and benchmarks
Retriever and generator errors remain coupled
cases.architecture: A dense retriever supplies passages to a sequence-to-sequence generator.
cases.approach: Condition generation on retrieved non-parametric memory.
tradeoffs: Evidence can be updated independently
Retrieval, context assembly, and generation add failure surfaces
failures_or_risks: Retrieved material can be irrelevant, stale, unsafe, or ignored
cases.reported_outcomes: The paper reported gains on selected knowledge-intensive tasks in its setup.
lessons: Evaluate retrieval and generation separately and jointly
Preserve provenance
cases.limitations: The original benchmark setup is not a production recipe.

cases.title: Hybrid retrieval and reranking are separable decisions
cases.problem: One retrieval signal may miss either lexical matches or semantic equivalents.
cases.context: BM25, dense passage retrieval, late interaction, and cross-encoder reranking research.
constraints: Dataset-sensitive ranking effects
Added stages increase latency and operational complexity
cases.architecture: Candidate generation using lexical and/or dense retrieval, followed by optional reranking.
cases.approach: Measure each stage with retrieval metrics before testing answer quality.
tradeoffs: Broader candidate recall
More index, model, and latency cost
failures_or_risks: Strong downstream prose can hide weak retrieval
Benchmark gains may not transfer
cases.reported_outcomes: The cited papers report ranking improvements on their evaluated benchmarks and configurations.
lessons: Treat chunking, candidate generation, and reranking as independent experiment variables
cases.limitations: No single retriever or reranker is declared universally best.

cases.title: LLM judges exhibit systematic biases
cases.problem: Scalable automated judging can be mistaken for objective ground truth.
cases.context: MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena evaluation research.
constraints: Specific judge prompts and models
Human agreement is itself contextual
cases.architecture: Pairwise or rubric-based model grading compared with human judgments.
cases.approach: Measure judge agreement and inspect position, verbosity, and self-enhancement biases.
tradeoffs: Lower-cost repeated grading
Judge dependence and correlated errors
failures_or_risks: Position and style can influence scores
A judge can share the system's blind spots
cases.reported_outcomes: The paper reported useful agreement in its setup while documenting important biases and limitations.
lessons: Calibrate automated graders
Keep human adjudication for high-stakes or ambiguous cases
cases.limitations: Judge quality changes with rubric, model, sampling, and task.

cases.title: Dolma documents a large pretraining-data pipeline
cases.problem: Large training corpora need auditable sourcing, filtering, deduplication, and documentation.
cases.context: The open Dolma corpus and its published construction report.
constraints: Very large web-derived corpus
Documentation does not eliminate embedded bias, rights, or privacy risk
cases.architecture: Multi-source acquisition followed by language, quality, safety, and deduplication processing.
cases.approach: Publish dataset composition, pipeline decisions, and limitations with artifacts.
tradeoffs: Reproducibility and scale
Filtering decisions can remove useful material or retain harmful content
failures_or_risks: Contamination and duplication can inflate evaluation
Web data carries provenance and consent concerns
cases.reported_outcomes: The authors released a documented multi-trillion-token corpus and described its processing pipeline.
lessons: Treat data lineage and split integrity as model-system requirements
cases.limitations: A published corpus is evidence of process, not blanket authorization for every use.

cases.title: Aya makes multilingual coverage an explicit data decision
cases.problem: Instruction-tuning resources and evaluation often concentrate on English.
cases.context: Aya's multilingual instruction dataset and model research.
constraints: Uneven language resources
Language coverage is not equivalent to cultural or domain adequacy
cases.architecture: Multilingual instruction data assembled from human and synthetic contributions, with model evaluation across languages.
cases.approach: Document language distribution, collection routes, and model results.
tradeoffs: Broader language access
Variable data quality and representativeness
failures_or_risks: Aggregate scores can conceal weak languages
Translation can erase local context
cases.reported_outcomes: The project reported multilingual instruction-following results for its released data and models.
lessons: Stratify data and evaluation by language
Do not infer authority from language fluency
cases.limitations: Results are model- and language-specific and require local validation.

cases.title: Tulu 3 treats post-training as a measured recipe
cases.problem: Post-training gains can be hard to attribute when data, stages, and evaluation are opaque.
cases.context: Open Tulu 3 post-training research and artifacts.
constraints: Specific base models, data mixtures, compute, and benchmarks
Benchmark improvements do not imply domain readiness
cases.architecture: A staged recipe spanning supervised finetuning, preference learning, reinforcement learning, and evaluation.
cases.approach: Publish recipe components and compare checkpoints across evaluation suites.
tradeoffs: More controllable behavior
Greater data, compute, and evaluation complexity
failures_or_risks: Stage interactions complicate causal attribution
Public benchmarks can be contaminated or incomplete
cases.reported_outcomes: The authors report improvements for their model family and recipe on named evaluations.
lessons: Freeze a baseline and preserve stage-level artifacts
Record the full data and training recipe
cases.limitations: A research recipe is not a turnkey operational standard.

cases.title: PEFT and QLoRA reduce the adaptation resource envelope
cases.problem: Full-parameter finetuning can exceed available accelerator memory and artifact budgets.
cases.context: LoRA and QLoRA methods, plus maintained PEFT tooling.
constraints: Quality depends on model, task, rank, quantization, and recipe
Lower trainable parameter count does not remove serving or evaluation cost
cases.architecture: Frozen base weights with trainable low-rank adapters; QLoRA backpropagates through a quantized base.
cases.approach: Adapt a smaller parameter subset and compare against the frozen baseline.
tradeoffs: Lower adaptation memory and smaller deltas
Adapter composition, compatibility, and merge behavior add lifecycle complexity
failures_or_risks: A small training loss does not demonstrate retained behavior
Quantized training may change numerical behavior
cases.reported_outcomes: The papers report substantial resource reductions with competitive results in their evaluated settings.
lessons: Choose the smallest adaptation that clears measured acceptance criteria
Version tokenizer, base, adapter, and merge state together
cases.limitations: No universal equivalence to full finetuning is claimed.

cases.title: DPO simplifies one preference-optimization path
cases.problem: RLHF pipelines can require a reward model and unstable reinforcement-learning optimization.
cases.context: Direct Preference Optimization research and maintained TRL implementation guidance.
constraints: Requires preference pairs and a reference policy formulation
Outcome depends on data quality and objective settings
cases.architecture: Direct optimization of a classification-style preference objective relative to a reference model.
cases.approach: Optimize preferred over rejected responses without a separately fitted reward model in the original formulation.
tradeoffs: Simpler training stack
Can optimize dataset artifacts or narrow preferences
failures_or_risks: Reward or benchmark gains can mask regressions
Preference labels may encode annotator bias
cases.reported_outcomes: The paper reports competitive preference-alignment results on its evaluated tasks.
lessons: Audit preference provenance
Use retention, safety, and judge-calibration controls
cases.limitations: Method evidence does not establish domain values or universal safety.

cases.title: PagedAttention exposes KV-cache allocation as a serving problem
cases.problem: Variable-length generation makes KV-cache memory large and fragmented under concurrent serving.
cases.context: vLLM/PagedAttention research and maintained serving documentation.
constraints: GPU-serving workloads and evaluated model families
Throughput depends on hardware, batching, sequence distribution, and software version
cases.architecture: KV-cache blocks managed with paging-inspired allocation and continuous batching.
cases.approach: Reduce memory waste and share blocks where possible while scheduling active sequences.
tradeoffs: Higher potential utilization
Scheduler complexity and latency interactions
failures_or_risks: Headline throughput may not transfer
Tail latency and output equivalence still require local tests
cases.reported_outcomes: The paper reports throughput improvements over named baselines in its experimental environment.
lessons: Benchmark the actual arrival and sequence-length distribution
Separate prefill, decode, throughput, and tail latency
cases.limitations: Performance numbers are not portable promises.

cases.title: AWQ and GPTQ make compression an empirical behavior question
cases.problem: Model weights and compute can exceed the target serving envelope.
cases.context: Post-training weight quantization research and maintained inference documentation.
constraints: Layer, bit-width, calibration, kernel, and hardware dependent
Aggregate perplexity is not application acceptance
cases.architecture: Low-bit weight representations with calibration or salience-aware choices, executed by compatible kernels.
cases.approach: Compress candidate artifacts, benchmark system performance, and rerun behavioral evaluations.
tradeoffs: Lower memory and potentially higher throughput
Quality drift and kernel/hardware compatibility
failures_or_risks: Some tasks or languages may regress disproportionately
Nominal bit width does not determine end-to-end speed
cases.reported_outcomes: The cited papers report accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs for their evaluated models and hardware.
lessons: Treat each compressed artifact as a new release candidate
Measure quality, latency, memory, and cost together
cases.limitations: No compression method is universally lossless or fastest.

cases.title: Managed-model deprecation is a lifecycle input
cases.problem: A managed model identifier or endpoint can be retired or migrated on a provider schedule.
cases.context: A current official API deprecation page used only as an example of change management.
constraints: Provider-specific schedule
Dates and replacement guidance are volatile
cases.architecture: Application contract and evaluation suite wrapped around a replaceable managed-model dependency.
cases.approach: Monitor official notices, pin identifiers where supported, qualify replacements, and maintain rollback or fallback plans.
tradeoffs: Managed access reduces infrastructure ownership
External lifecycle and behavior changes remain dependencies
failures_or_risks: Unqualified migrations can alter quality, latency, cost, or safety behavior
cases.reported_outcomes: No product outcome is asserted; the official page demonstrates that deprecation schedules exist and change.
lessons: Version behavior-facing dependencies and keep the release gate provider-neutral
cases.limitations: Illustrative lifecycle evidence, not a provider recommendation or stable schedule snapshot.

cases.title: Prompt injection is a system trust-boundary failure
cases.problem: Untrusted content can carry instructions that compete with the application's intended control path.
cases.context: NIST generative-AI/adversarial-ML guidance, primary prompt-injection research, and official application-safety guidance.
constraints: Threats evolve
Controls depend on tools, data sensitivity, and deployment context
cases.architecture: LLM application receiving user, retrieved, and tool-derived content across trust boundaries.
cases.approach: Separate instructions from data, minimize privileges, validate outputs and actions, test adversarial cases, and require human authority where needed.
tradeoffs: Additional isolation and review reduce autonomy or convenience
No single prompt eliminates the threat
failures_or_risks: Data exfiltration
Unauthorized tool action
Instruction override
cases.reported_outcomes: The sources characterize risks and recommended controls; no guaranteed prevention rate is claimed.
lessons: Treat model output as untrusted
Keep authorization outside the model
cases.limitations: Security ownership remains with the appropriate security and system authorities.
